differences.text: Below the mobile breakpoint (767 px and narrower by default, from the shell) the bar collapses to the heading, the end content and a `tct-mobile-nav-toggle` (unless the shell has `no-mobile-toggle`); the start and centre items go to the shell's mobile drawer above the side navigation with a rule between, as copies shown by an internal `tct-top-nav-drawer` (a click on a copy is forwarded to the original, and the copies are rebuilt when the originals change). A `tct-mobile-nav` of your own keeps the full bar.

The resting ink of the items is `--color-text-secondary` and their icons rest on the top-nav adornment role; each interaction state (hover, keyboard focus, pressed, current page) switches to `--color-text-primary`. The owner's export of `--tecton-color-top-nav-text` (black or white at 50%) measures 4.0:1 on the light band and fails WCAG 1.4.3 for 14 px labels; the band itself keeps the top-nav background role. Contrast is tested in light and dark, at rest and in hover, focus, current and expanded states.
The top navigation draws no heading of its own and never truncates item labels with a tooltip; the `topbar` side navigation mode is not derived from it (an explicit `sideNavRenderContext` only).

tokenRequests.reason: The export value measures 4.0:1 on the light top-nav band (WCAG 1.4.3 needs 4.5:1 for 14 px text). The items use `--color-text-secondary` at rest (7.5:1 light, 8.4:1 dark) instead. If the owner wants the role itself to pass, the light value needs a higher alpha.

requests.reason: Upstream AppShell hands the side navigation content to the top navigation through `TopNavMobileContentContext` to build one combined drawer. A custom element cannot project one node into two places, so `tct-top-nav` adds a `tct-top-nav-drawer` satellite (`slot="drawer"`) to the shell, which lists copies of the start and centre items above the side navigation and forwards their clicks. No shell change is needed; if the shell later exposes an API for drawer contributions, the satellite can use it.

differences.text: Disclosure navigation, not an ARIA menu (upstream navigation-destinations guidance): a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` shows a labelled group of links, with no `role="menu"`, `aria-haspopup` or `menuitem`. Enter and Space toggle (upstream never closes from the keyboard), a keyboard open moves focus to the first link, a pointer open leaves focus on the button, Tab moves through the links and out of the panel (which closes it), and only one panel is open at a time.

The panel aligns to the region of the bar the menu sits in (start, centre or end) and mirrors in RTL; positioning is the shared `PositionController` (CSS anchor positioning with a Floating UI fallback in Tier 2). In the mobile drawer the menu is a collapsible section whose header toggles the links.
No typeahead and no roving `menuitem` focus (`useListFocus`, `useTypeahead`): they are menu semantics, which the disclosure pattern does not have.

differences.text: Disclosure navigation like `tct-top-nav-menu`: the panel is a labelled group of links (a browsing grid of links is the documented anti-case for `role="menu"`). A hover-open leaves focus on the button; a click or key open moves focus in.

The panel is anchored to the whole bar (the implicit anchor of the top navigation), not to the button: below the bar, at most 960 px wide, aligned to the start, the centre or the end of the bar by the region the item sits in, mirrored in RTL, and scrolling inside when the space below is short. With the Floating UI fallback (Tier 2) the panel keeps an 8 px gutter to the viewport edge.
